rv.q: But, directed by Amanda Huxtable, it is enormous fun, full of heart and undeniably entertaining. If this first play is a measure of his ambition, Powell intends to be a crowd-pleaser. Takeaway wouldn’t be out of place in the unabashedly popular Royal Court across town.
A little finessing of the staging, pace and vocal delivery wouldn’t go amiss – but it certainly hits its target.
The play itself, however, lacks a depth of flavour.
Those in the audience, nearer to the stage, were laughing at the many jokes delivered by the script and were able to enjoy the performance but this reviewer sadly was unable to.

cn.t: Powell's warm-hearted family drama about a Liverpool Caribbean café charms with its community spirit and universal themes, though critics find the structure loose and story lacking depth.
